title: Normalized native pullback tensor comparison and its proper counit mate
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Use the native abelian Weil sheaves, ordinary ambient derived categories and bounded constructible subcategories of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], with the actual relative tensor and its K-flat total-complex models from [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations], the actual pullback, sheaf tensor, summand insertions and tensor models of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-operations], with the conventions of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-presentation-data], and the open tensor restriction normalization of [def-sf-generic-open-tensor-presentation]. Let $p_0:Z_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. A normalized native pullback tensor comparison consists of a natural isomorphism $\mu:p_0^*(-\otimes^L-)\xrightarrow{\sim}p_0^*(-)\otimes^Lp_0^*(-)$ together with a sheaf, total-complex and K-flat presentation. Every functor, tensor, K-flat predicate, representative model and summand insertion in the presentation is the recorded native one; the total map agrees with its sheaf map on every summand, and its localization is precisely $\mu$ on all K-flat pairs. The sheaf map after forgetting Frobenius is the existing balanced module pullback tensor map $b\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. For such a comparison define its projection mate at ambient derived $A,T$ to be the transpose, under the actual derived pullback/direct-image adjunction, of $\mu_{Rp_{0*}A,T}$ followed by $\varepsilon_A\otimes1$. No invertibility of this projection mate is part of the definition.
